title: Alien Dictionary
summary: Recover an alphabet's letter order from a list of words sorted in that alphabet, or report that none exists.

tests.explain: "qr" before "qs" gives r < s. "qs" before "ps" gives q < p. "ps" before "psr" says nothing (a prefix comes first anyway). "psr" before "rq" gives p < r. The only order is q, p, r, s.
"mo" before "om" means m < o, but "om" before "mm" means o < m. Both can't be true, so return "".
A word can never come after a longer word that it is a prefix of, whatever the alphabet, so the list is invalid: "".

hints: Compare each word only with the next one. The first position where they differ tells you one letter comes before another; nothing after that position tells you anything.
Those facts are edges of a directed graph on letters. Every letter that appears in any word is a node, even if it has no edges. Any topological order is a valid alphabet.
Return "" in two cases: a word is followed by its own proper prefix ("abc" then "ab"), or Kahn's algorithm can't place every letter because of a cycle. Add each edge once so in-degrees stay right.

complexity.time: O(C): C is the total number of characters; at most 26 letters and 26² edges
complexity.space: O(1) beyond the input: the graph has at most 26 nodes and 26² edges
